Summary: Benchmark KRYLO against the J.P. Morgan 2026 Global M&A Mid-Year Outlook (validation, no spec)
Description: 1) Original intent: test whether existing KRYLO independently surfaces the structural system the J.P. Morgan 2026 Global M&A Mid-Year Outlook describes (Founder, 2026-10-06). Method: report claims -> candidate KRYLO queries -> real KRYLO results -> gap classification. This is a validation exercise, not a new capability. 2) Acceptance criteria: every claim in the claims table has a run result and a final classification: No change (KRYLO captures it) / Defect (evidence exists, KRYLO fails to establish the relationship) / Data-source gap (KRYLO lacks the evidence) / Spec (the architecture cannot represent the structure). Classification is based on reviewed per-domain observations and evidence, not only the brief text. A spec is written only if a row classifies as Spec. Pages 7 onward of the PDF are added only for genuinely new structural claims. 3) Current implementation state: claims table for pages 1-6 committed (specs/benchmark-jpmorgan-mid-year-2026-claims-table.md, commit 5ad972b); all 14 queries run on Dev 2026-10-06 (run log committed 7a44a05). Result so far: 13 of 14 returned ambient field-only output with no subject resolved; two queries parsed generic nouns as structural participants; Q11 (NVIDIA) resolved with 24 subject-bound observations and 4 canonical relationships (beneficial-ownership disclosures), and showed no hyperscaler-capex to supplier dependency. Classifications are provisional (based on the first ~2,600 characters of the left column). Next: inspect per-domain observations and evidence for each row to separate defect from data gap. 4) Dependencies: Dev running with the access-code login; related KRYL-1359 and KRYL-1360 (subject-scope loss, thematic concepts treated as entities), KRYL-1369 (brief wording), pages 7+ of specs/jpmorgan-2026-global-m-and-a-mid-year-outlook-v3.pdf. 5) Superseded by a newer ticket: none known. 6) Maps to current product model: yes; tests detection of structural asymmetry on an external benchmark, no prediction (section 21). Non-goals: no speculative spec; do not rerun the queries unless a specific evidence gap requires it.
